decisions.quote: In the present project, we sought to replicate the study by Imel et al. (2014b) within two large samples (N = 208 and N = 204) of clinical interactions with real patients from two independent studies of Swiss French-speaking samples.
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly replicates Imel et al. (2014b) (10.1037/a0034943), whereas the shipped row mistakenly matched the abstract's 'Imel et al. 2014' citation to the sibling reference Imel et al. (2014a) (10.1037/a0036158), which is only cited as background context.

decisions.quote: Findings showed no support for our hypothesis that mean F0 synchrony between clinicians and patients would be higher in high-empathy sessions based on empathy ratings measured using traditional, labor intensive, behavioral coding. This lack of replication was consistent for both clinical samples (brief MI with young men and general practice consultation), both behavioral coding instruments (Empathy global rating from the MISC and TES scale), and both levels of analysis (session-level and minute-level synchrony).
decisions.reason: With original identity resolved to Imel et al. (2014b), both shipped and blind coding agree the replication failed across both samples, both empathy measures, and both levels of analysis.
